title: Edge Request Anchor and Loss-Tolerant Carrier for Trace Stitching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an edge-side lightweight request anchoring carrier that survives partial header loss and best-effort stitches spans across unreliable transports (websockets, mobile SDK retries, legacy proxies).

Background: We frequently see traces drop or fragment at edge boundaries where proxies or mobile networks drop non-standard headers. Existing propagators assume header fidelity and end up producing disconnected traces or creating new root spans. This ticket implements a compact anchor (request watermark + minimal fingerprint) that can be carried in both HTTP headers and a binary carrier for websocket frames, and a small server-side reconciliation layer that attempts to stitch separated spans using timestamp and fingerprint heuristics.

Scope:
- Add an SDK-level carrier encoder/decoder (32-byte compact anchor) that:
  • Encodes origin id, truncated request-id hash, sequence counter, and a 16-bit checksum.
  • Falls back gracefully if header space is missing (writes only to binary carriers when available).
  • Enables opaque header short-form (x-rw-anchor) and binary frame metadata for WS/gRPC.
- Edge proxy middleware that:
  • Normalizes incoming anchors from multiple header encodings.
  • Attaches an internal routed-anchor (edge-node-id + ingress time) for downstream services to use.
- Stitching reconciler in request-observability service that:
  • Matches orphan spans to anchors using time windows, id-hashes, and sequence counters.
  • Marks stitched traces with confidence score and emits stitching events for diagnostics.
- Backwards compatibility: must interoperate with existing W3C traceparent and our legacy x-rw-request headers; avoid creating duplicate root spans.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (Node, Python, Go) can emit the compact anchor in HTTP and WS frames.
- Edge proxy normalizes >=95% of received anchors in our canary region (us-west-2).
- Stitcher reduces orphan-rate by >=50% for canary traffic (>10k requests/day) with <1% false-stitch rate in synthetic tests.
- End-to-end tests and staging rollout with traffic shadowing pass without false-positive duplicate-root creation.

Non-goals: Persistent full-trace reconstruction for arbitrary data loss; this is a best-effort, low-overhead improvement to trace coverage and usability in the console.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on compact 32-byte format to keep overhead low for mobile. Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood/obs/edge-anchor-design

2025-01-20 - Arjun Patel: Prototyped anchor encoder/decoder in the Node SDK. Initial binary format: 8b origin, 8b truncated req-hash, 4b seq, 2b checksum, 10b reserved. Benchmarks: +12 bytes header overhead on avg. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2107
2025-01-23 - SRE (review): Concern about header collision with CDNs; agreed to add short header name x-rw-a and a feature flag to opt-in at edge proxies.
2025-01-28 - Design review: UX in Console: add a stitching badge on traces with confidence score; mockups in Drive: https://drive.redwood/designs/trace-stitching-mock

2025-01-30 - Arjun Patel: Integration tests (staging): created harness to simulate partial header drop and websocket frame loss. Stitcher matched 62% of orphaned spans in synthetic run. Next: tune checksum threshold and time-window matching algorithm.
2025-02-01 - QA: Found edge case where retry storms can cause duplicate anchors. Mitigation: include sequence counter jitter and id aging TTL. Added test case #ST-98 to test plan.
2025-02-02 - PM (Nora Alvarez): Approved canary rollout plan pending SRE runbooks. Add metrics: anchor_received, anchor_normalized, stitch_success, stitch_confidence_histogram, false_stitch_alerts.
